children: AI spending among the top 1% of businesses by AI expenditure declined in August, adding a new wrinkle to the rapid expansion in corporate demand for artificial intelligence.
The top 1% of businesses spent $7.2K per employee per month on AI in August, down 10% from a July peak of $8K, according to Ramp AI Index data shared by Ara Kharazian, lead economist at Ramp.

Kharazian said the data showed “more cracks in the AI thesis,” with several spending drivers appearing to be topping out. He attributed the decline to “model wars,” rather than the availability of open Chinese models.
“Price cuts + a growing share of spend is shifting to standard and lite models,” Kharazian said, adding that those models are already cheaper than frontier models.

The pullback among the biggest AI spenders contrasted with continued increases across broader groups of businesses. Spending among the top 10% reached about $680 per employee per month in August, while median AI spending rose to about $14 per employee per month, according to the Ramp AI Index chart.
The chart showed AI spending per employee increasing substantially across all three groups from January 2024 through August 2026, although the top 1% saw a notable decline from its July peak.

The pattern suggests the latest pullback among the heaviest AI spenders reflects pricing and model-mix dynamics, rather than necessarily signaling a broad decline in AI spending. Ramp's measure includes LLM subscriptions, coding agents, API tokens, and GPU cloud spending.

title: AI spending cools at biggest-spending firms as model wars intensify
